evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, wording, values and figure briefs are newly authored. The mapped P2 leaves inform only the demand for reasonable mass and volume estimates within defensible ranges.

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: prior-learning retrieval to scale selection, benchmark justification, grouped estimation and an integrated spatial estimate

questions.prompt: From the previous lesson, state the two parts that make up every physical quantity.
Which is the most reasonable estimate for the mass of a loaded school bag?
Which is the most reasonable estimate for the time taken for one blink of an eye?
A large apple is compared with a cube of side about 5 cm. Which is the most reasonable estimate for the apple's volume?
Make a reasonable estimate, in metres, of the height of a classroom door. Name a familiar benchmark, compare the door with it and use your comparison to justify the estimate.

The diagram shows a tied bundle of identical exercise books and gives a reasonable estimated mass for one book. Use the diagram to estimate the mass of the bundle. Explain why the answer is an estimate, then give one physical check showing that its scale is believable.

figure.purpose: Support grouped benchmark reasoning without revealing the multiplication or result
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white line drawing of a tied bundle of 12 identical exercise books. Show the books as three visible groups of four and label one book with estimated mass 0.25 kg. Do not show any total or arithmetic.
figure.alt_text: A tied bundle contains 12 identical exercise books, each estimated to have mass 0.25 kg.

questions.prompt: The diagram gives three approximate dimensions of a rectangular laboratory storage box and shows a 10 cm cube. Estimate the box volume in cm³ by multiplying its three approximate dimensions. In your final record, identify the numerical magnitude and the unit, explain why the bare number would be incomplete, and use the 10 cm cube to check the scale.

figure.purpose: Assess spatial organisation of three approximate dimensions and a cube-based scale check
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white line drawing of a rectangular storage box. Place dimension arrows labelled roughly 40 cm, 30 cm and 25 cm on the correct perpendicular edges. Beside it draw one unshaded 10 cm cube as a check reference. Do not show the volume calculation or answer.
figure.alt_text: A rectangular storage box has approximate dimensions 40 cm by 30 cm by 25 cm, with a 10 cm cube shown for scale.
